narrative.overview:
A clean editorial product page laid on near-white paper. The ground is never pure white, headlines are a sans set tight and in two tones, controls are small and square-shouldered, and the only colour in the room belongs to the real credit cards and the five category pastels. The owner pinned the world to the Zaro reference on 28 October 2026: near-white ground, grey and lavender demo panels, a warm charcoal band near the end, a dark footer.

The system has two kinds of surface and treats them differently. **Persuade** (landing, sign in) proves the answer instead of describing it: the hero's right half is the working category picker, drawn as an isometric stack of the real card faces, and the credits section is the real CheckmarkRow being ticked by a pointer. **Operate** (wallet, tracker, calculators, compare, settings) keeps its layouts and inherits the same tokens; there, scanability and consistency outrank expression and the brand lives in type, spacing and radius, not decoration.

Density is calm. Sections breathe (80px, 112px at desktop), panels pad at 20px to 28px, and grouping comes from hairline borders and tonal steps before it comes from shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white ground in three tonal steps (page, raised surface, demo panel).
Geist at every size; display is weight 500 with negative tracking.
Two-tone headlines: the claim in ink, the consequence in muted.
Square-shouldered radii (12 / 8 / 6); pill only for tracks and dots.
One warm charcoal band that closes the marketing pages.
Colour belongs to cards and categories; there is no brand accent hue.
The real components do the demonstrating, in motion.

rules.name: The Near-White Rule
rules.body: Never pure white, never pure black. The page is `bg`, raised is `surface`, a demo sits on `panel`; depth is a tonal step first.

rules.name: The Cards Are The Colour Rule
rules.body: No accent hue exists. Saturated colour comes from card art and category pastels only, so a pastel always means a category.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: A headline states its claim in ink and its consequence in muted (`band-muted` on the band). One sentence, two weights of attention.

rules.name: The Mono Measures Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for measurements and axis labels only, and loads only in the marketing layout, so the app never pays for it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular everywhere by default, so money and point balances line up in a column.

rules.name: The Border Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate with a hairline or a tonal step first. No stacked shadows, no coloured halos.

rules.name: The Square Shoulder Rule
rules.body: Nothing picks a radius outside this scale, and pill is never a button or chip shape.

dos: **Do** put every colour, radius, duration and curve in `app/globals.css` and reference the token.
**Do** write headlines two-tone: claim in ink, consequence in muted.
**Do** keep the ground near-white in three steps (`bg`, `surface`, `panel`).
**Do** demonstrate with the real component, in motion if it helps, rather than a picture of it.
**Do** say the answer in words next to any visual that encodes it; a highlighted card alone leaves the user to work out why it won.
**Do** give every interactive element hover, press, focus and disabled states, and check both themes.
**Do** use container queries when the available width is not the viewport's.
**Do** write real sample data and label it as sample on the page.
donts: **Don't** use an em dash or en dash in any visible string. Not one, anywhere.
**Don't** introduce an accent hue, a gradient fill, gradient text or a glowing blob; colour belongs to cards and categories.
**Don't** use a pill radius on a button or chip, or any radius outside the scale.
**Don't** use Geist Mono for anything but measurements and axis labels, or load it in the app layout.
**Don't** put an uppercase wide-tracking eyebrow above a heading; the two-tone headline carries the section.
**Don't** nest a widget inside a widget.
**Don't** use a status dot the reader cannot decode, number sections, or add scroll cues.
**Don't** build a fake product screenshot out of divs.
**Don't** centre everything; reach for a deliberate asymmetry.
**Don't** ship a shadcn component in its default styling.
